articles.title: Curtains for Ravindra Jadeja in ODIs? All-rounder drops out of 2027 World Cup plans
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: It is increasingly possible that Ravindra Jadeja has played his last ODI for India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It is increasingly possible that Ravindra Jadeja has played his last ODI for India. The veteran all-rounder was left out of the playing XI for the third match after a below-par return in the first two ODIs against the West Indies. Captain Shubman Gill maintained that Jadeja was rested not dropped, but the writing is very much on the wall for the experienced all-rounder in the format."I don’t think Jaddu bhai was dropped. We rested him because we had an opportunity today to give game time to other players. When a series is only three matches long, it becomes very difficult to give experience to players sitting outside," Gill said in the post-match press conference after India’s defeat in the third ODI in New Chandigarh.Jadeja picked up only two wickets in the first two matches and did not get an opportunity to bat. Since the 2023 ODI World Cup, Jadeja has played only 15 of the 32 ODIs India have played. He has taken 14 wickets at an average of 47.92 and an economy rate of 5.20. His bowling returns have declined sharply in recent times.Before the Guwahati ODI, Jadeja had managed only one wicket in his previous seven ODIs, although that was not entirely unexpected. Given his bowling style and recent pitch conditions, he was unlikely to regularly dismantle batting line-ups in ODIs unless conditions significantly assisted him.Since the 2025 Champions Trophy, where he was part of India’s spin quartet, Jadeja has taken only five wickets in eight matches, with his economy rate going beyond six runs per over.He is not in India’s scheme of things for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Axar and Washington were playing in the Asian Games, whereas Harsh Dubey and Shahbaz Ahmed are at the CoE because they were injured.His batting numbers do little to strengthen his case. Jadeja has not scored an ODI fifty in the last six years. Since the 2023 World Cup, he has made 149 runs in 10 innings. While Jadeja has never been viewed primarily as a batter in ODIs, his batting was an important part of his overall value to the team.In 142 ODI innings across 212 matches, Jadeja has crossed the fifty-run mark only 13 times. His principal role in the format, however, has been that of a bowler capable of controlling the run rate. At his best, he could hold up one end, complete his 10-over spell for around 45-50 runs and chip in with a wicket or two.That reliability, though, has not been as evident recently.Jadeja is now fifth in the pecking order among India’s spin-bowling all-rounders, behind Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Harsh Dubey and Shahbaz Ahmed."He is not in India’s scheme of things for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Axar and Washington were playing in the Asian Games, whereas Harsh Dubey and Shahbaz Ahmed are at the CoE because they were injured," a source tracking the developments told TimesofIndia.com."And when it comes to the left-arm spin all-rounder option, Axar is ahead of Jadeja. Axar has more wicket-taking ability and can bat as a floater from No. 4 to No. 7 in the middle overs. By no means is he inferior when it comes to fielding," the source added.For me, Jadeja has always been a utility player. He has definitely improved as a bowler over the last six months.The numbers over the last 12 months also underline the changing pecking order. Jadeja has taken only one wicket in seven ODIs during this period, leaving him with a bowling average of more than 350. Across the six ODIs against New Zealand and South Africa, he generally did not complete his full quota of 10 overs, with the Thiruvananthapuram ODI against the West Indies being the only exception.Axar Patel, meanwhile, has produced significantly better returns. He has taken eight wickets in six ODIs over the last 12 months, with a bowling average of 30.87, better than his career average of 32.73.After the Guwahati ODI, India’s spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule described Jadeja as a "utility player" and said the all-rounder had improved as a bowler over the previous six months."For me, Jadeja has always been a utility player. He has definitely improved as a bowler over the last six months," Bahutule said after the Guwahati ODI.However, the numbers since the 2023 World Cup favour Axar. He has taken 21 wickets in 19 matches at an economy rate of 4.53. Axar has taken a wicket every 45 balls, while Jadeja’s strike rate in his 15 appearances is 55.2, meaning he has taken a wicket every 55 balls.Jadeja’s batting role has also largely been confined to No. 7 or 8 of late, and he does not offer a significantly different skill set from the other options in contention. Axar, his most direct competitor, has carved out a more defined role as a spin-hitter.Since the 2023 World Cup final, Axar has scored 437 runs in 18 innings at an average of 29.13, including two fifties.There had been signs earlier that Jadeja’s position in the ODI set-up could come under pressure. Last year, former chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar suggested that India did not necessarily need Jadeja in Australian conditions, given the limited value of playing two left-arm spinners."He is very much in the plans. But there will be some competition for places. Of course, he was there in the Champions Trophy squad because we took those extra spinners with the conditions there. At the moment, we could only carry one and get some balance in the team with Washi and Kuldeep there as well. And I don’t think we are going to need more than that in Australia," Agarkar had said.South Africa, the hosts of the 2027 ODI World Cup alongside Zimbabwe and Namibia, could offer conditions that are similarly demanding for India’s spinners. With Jadeja no longer providing the same control with the ball and his batting returns not strong enough to compensate, the selectors appear to have several younger alternatives.Gill may insist that Jadeja was rested rather than dropped for the third ODI. But with Axar ahead of him, Washington Sundar offering another spin-bowling option and Harsh Dubey and Shahbaz Ahmed also in the mix, the reality is that Jadeja’s path back into India’s ODI plans is becoming increasingly difficult.The third ODI in New Chandigarh may, therefore, have been more significant for Jadeja than the Indian captain’s description of it as a rest suggests.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ECB abandons Rooney Rule in recruiting coaches for England teams
articles.summary: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) abandons use of the Rooney Rule in hiring coaches for national teams, saying its recruitment has "evolved".
articles.body:
The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has abandoned use of the Rooney Rule in hiring coaches for national teams, saying its recruitment has "evolved".

In 2018, the ECB committed to interviewing at least one applicant from an ethnic minority background for all coaching roles in the national men's, women's and disabled teams.

The commitment came five years before a report from the Independent Commission for Equity in Cricket (ICEC) concluded discrimination was "widespread" in the sport in England and Wales.

Since then, the ECB has repeatedly stated its aim for cricket to become "the most inclusive sport in the country".

Asked by BBC Sport about the hiring process for 16 roles connected to the England men's and women's teams since 2024, the ECB confirmed that not all appointments were made with the application of the Rooney Rule - and it is no longer routinely used in coaching recruitment.

The Rooney Rule was implemented in American football's NFL in 2003.

Named after NFL diversity committee chairman Dan Rooney, it requires clubs in American football to interview at least one ethnic minority candidate for each head coach or senior football operation vacancy.

An ECB spokesperson said: "We regularly review our recruitment practices, and our approach has evolved over the last eight years.

"Coach recruitment processes are tailored to the requirements of each role. Some appointments involve open recruitment processes, while others involve targeted searches for specialist skillsets, experience and leadership qualities. At times we recruit an individual, and at others we recruit a team."

Of the recruitments BBC Sport highlighted to the ECB, not all were coaches - some were roles of selector or director of cricket.

They included appointments made in the past week. On Monday, Richard Dawson, James Foster and Eric Simons joined the coaching staff of the men's Test team, and Michael Yardy was named as elite national batting lead.

Rew, 18, to captain England Lions in West Indies

England include red-ball game in India tour as Ashes prep

Crawley signs Kent extension after losing England deal

The ECB confirmed at least one ethnic minority candidate was part of the process when Stephen Fleming became Test head coach in July.

In April 2025, then director of women's cricket Clare Connor did not use an open recruitment process or the Rooney Rule when she named Charlotte Edwards head coach of the England women's team.

At the time, Connor told BBC Sport: "I think the Rooney Rule should be absolutely applied in all circumstances where it is deemed feasible. I don't think it's on the whim of the person recruiting or hiring.

"It is practise within the ECB across our pathway appointments and our senior appointments in England cricket that we apply the Rooney Rule."

In its statement issued to BBC Sport, the ECB continued: "In elite sport, the pool of candidates can be relatively small. As such, we use a range of approaches, including external recruitment specialists and the expertise of our internal teams, to identify the strongest possible candidates and ensure we consider coaches from a range of backgrounds.

"We remain committed to improving diversity and representation within cricket. We recognise there are differing views on the effectiveness of the Rooney Rule, and instead of applying that in every case, our experience has shown that strengthening the coaching and leadership pipeline, and increasing the number of ethnically diverse and female coaches progressing through the system, is the most effective way of securing long-term change.

"We believe that our continued commitment to the coaching pathway and development will have the greatest long-term impact on representation."

The ECB announced its intention to implement the Rooney Rule in May 2018. Almost three years later, in March 2021, the ICEC was announced in the wake of global movements such as Black Lives Matter and Me Too.

In 2023, the ICEC's report, called Holding Up a Mirror to Cricket, concluded racism, sexism, classism and elitism were rife in the game.

As part of its work to improve inclusion in cricket, the ECB has focussed on growing the number of female and ethnically diverse coaches at all levels. In 2025, the governing body funded more than 1,000 coaching bursaries, of which 22% were awarded to coaches from ethnically diverse backgrounds.

The ECB's coaching pathway has five steps - advanced and specialist are the two highest levels a coach can achieve.

Since 2021, 21% of the coaches taking the advanced level course and 19% of the coaches on the specialist course have been from ethnically diverse backgrounds.

articles.title: Why are India, Zimbabwe players wearing black armbands during 1st Women’s T20I?
articles.summary: India and Zimbabwe players wore black armbands during the first T20I between the two sides at the Shaheed Veer Narayan International Stadium in Raipur on
articles.body: India and Zimbabwe players wore black armbands during the first T20I between the two sides at the Shaheed Veer Narayan International Stadium in Raipur on Friday to honour former Zimbabwe cricketer and umpire Sarah Dambanevana, who passed away earlier this week.The players and match officials also observed a minute's silence before the start of play in her memory."The Indian Cricket Team, Zimbabwe Cricket Team and match officials are wearing black arm bands and observed a moment of silence in honour and memory of former Zimbabwe cricketer and umpire Sarah Dambanevana, following her recent passing," the BCCI said in a post on X.Dambanevana passed away following a brief illness. She represented Zimbabwe as a fast bowler before moving into umpiring, where she became one of the country's pioneering female match officials.In 2022, she became the first female umpire from Zimbabwe to join the ICC Development Umpires Panel. She received her first ICC appointment at the ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup in January 2023.At the age of 36, she had officiated in 72 senior international matches, including 10 men's T20Is, 14 women's ODIs and 48 women's T20Is.Her last match was the T20I between Ireland and Thailand on February 1, 2026, during the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 Global Qualifier in Nepal.Meanwhile, India opted to field against Zimbabwe in the first T20I of the three-match series in Raipur on Friday. The series marks the start of Smriti Mandhana's tenure as India's captain, while middle-order batter Niki Prasad is set to make her international debut.The series is also the first bilateral international contest between India and Zimbabwe.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill returns to Ranji Trophy, set to play Punjab's next match
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill will return to action for Punjab in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill will return to action for Punjab in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that Gill will play Punjab's second-round match against Chhattisgarh, starting on October 18.Gill missed Punjab's opening Ranji Trophy match against Assam in New Chandigarh. Former India U-19 captain Uday Saharan led Punjab in that game.Gill was named the ICC Men's Player of the Month for a record fifth time following his impressive performances in the ODI series against the West Indies.He matched West Indies captain Hayley Matthews, who has also won the award five times. Gill, 27, had earlier received the honour in January and September 2023, and February and July 2025.Gill scored 110 in the first ODI against the West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram.He then smashed 223 off 133 balls, recording the fastest double-century ever. His innings helped his team chase down a target of 406 with eight wickets in hand and 39 balls to spare.India’s ODI squad for New Zealand tour to be picked soonThe India T20I squad for the New Zealand tour has already been announced. The squad for the five-match ODI series on the same tour will be selected soon.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia told TOI on Wednesday that the ODI squad would be picked in the next two to three days.“We will select India’s ODI team in the next two or three days,” Saikia said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India Test and ODI squads for New Zealand tour announced: Who is in, who is out?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The BCCI selection committee has announced India's ODI and Test squads for the upcoming tour of New Zealand.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The BCCI selection committee has announced India's ODI and Test squads for the upcoming tour of New Zealand. India will play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests on the tour.Fast bowlers Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj have returned to the Test squad. Shubman Gill will lead India in the first three ODIs, while Shreyas Iyer will captain the team in the last two matches.Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj return to Test squadAkash Deep and Anshul Kamboj have been included in India's 16-member Test squad for the two-match series against New Zealand.Akash Deep recently returned to action after recovering from a lower-back stress fracture. His last appearance for India came during the 2025 tour of England, where he impressed with his performances.Kamboj, meanwhile, returns to the team after being dropped following his Test debut in England last year.DateTimeMatchVenue19-Nov-263:30 AM IST1st TestWellington27-Nov-263:30 AM IST2nd TestChristchurchBoth pacers are also part of the India A squad that will play three multi-day matches against New Zealand A before the Test series. The team management will look to give them match practice ahead of the Tests.Gurnoor Brar, who has performed well recently, has not been included in the Test squad. Wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant has been selected subject to fitness clearance as he continues to recover from a left rib injury.India's pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah will feature only in the Test series during the New Zealand tour.Shreyas Iyer to captain India in last two ODIsShubman Gill will lead India in the first three ODIs before Shreyas Iyer takes over for the final two matches.Iyer will be Gill's deputy in the first three games, while Ishan Kishan has been named vice-captain for the fourth and fifth ODIs.The change in leadership comes as Gill shifts his focus to the Test series, which begins on November 19. KL Rahul, who is part of the first three ODI matches, will also turn his attention to red-ball cricket.Senior batters Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli will be available for all five ODIs. All-rounders Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel and Naman Dhir are also part of both ODI squads.Kumar Kushagra gets maiden ODI call-upWicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra has received his maiden India call-up for the final two ODIs. Fast bowler Yash Thakur has also earned his first ODI call-up.Left-handed batter Tilak Varma returns to the ODI squad after last playing 50-over cricket in December 2025. Pacer Auqib Nabi has also been included for the last two matches.Ravindra Jadeja has been left out of the ODI squads. Senior pacers Mohammed Shami and Bhuvneshwar Kumar have also not been included.Bhuvneshwar was added to India's squad for the fifth T20I against the West Indies in Bengaluru and is set to feature in the T20I series against New Zealand, starting on October 22.India vs New Zealand ODI scheduleThe five-match ODI series will begin on November 4 at Eden Park in Auckland. The second match will be played at Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 7, followed by the third ODI at Seddon Park in Hamilton on November 10.The final two matches will take place at Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15. All five ODIs are scheduled to begin at 7:30 AM IST.DateTimeMatchVenue04-Nov-267:30 AM IST1st ODIAuckland07-Nov-267:30 AM IST2nd ODIWellington10-Nov-267:30 AM IST3rd ODIHamilton13-Nov-267:30 AM IST4th ODIMount Maunganui15-Nov-267:30 AM IST5th ODIMount MaunganuiIndia's ODI squad for first three matchesShubman Gill (captain), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (vice-captain), KL Rahul (wicketkeeper), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Ishan Kishan (wicketkeeper), Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna* and Kuldeep Yadav.India's ODI squad for fourth and fifth matchesShreyas Iyer (captain), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan (wicketkeeper and vice-captain), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Kumar Kushagra (wicketkeeper), Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur and Kuldeep Yadav.India's Test squad for New Zealand tourShubman Gill (captain), Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul (vice-captain), Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant (wicketkeeper)*, Dhruv Jurel (wicketkeeper), Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep, Sai Sudharsan, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav and Mohammed Siraj.Prasidh Krishna and Rishabh Pant are subject to fitness clearance.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jasprit Bumrah returns, Kuldeep Yadav retains place as India make a host of changes for New Zealand Tests
articles.summary: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Friday announced a 15-member squad for India's two-Test series against New Zealand in November.
articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Friday announced a 15-member squad for India's two-Test series against New Zealand in November.Jasprit Bumrah has returned to the Test squad after missing India's previous series against Sri Lanka. He was initially named in that squad but was later withdrawn due to injury.Rishabh Pant, who missed India A's tour of New Zealand after suffering an injury during the domestic Irani Trophy, has also been included, subject to fitness.Fast bowlers Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj have been named in the squad. Akash Deep recently returned to action after recovering from a stress fracture. He last played for India during the 2025 tour of England, where he impressed. Kamboj, meanwhile, was dropped after making his debut in England last year.Kuldeep Yadav has retained his place in the squad, while left-arm spinner Manav Suthar has missed out.The first Test will begin in Wellington on November 19, four days after the five-match ODI series ends. The second Test is scheduled to start in Christchurch on November 27. The series will be important to India's chances of reaching the World Test Championship final.India have also announced two squads for the five-match ODI series against New Zealand. Shreyas Iyer will lead the team in the final two ODIs, while regular captain Shubman Gill will turn his attention to red-ball cricket ahead of the Test series.Wicket-keeper Kumar Kushagra has earned his maiden India call up with a spot in the ODI team for the last two games.Veteran Ravindra Jadeja has been left out of the ODI side.In total, India play five T20s, as many ODIs and two Test on the New Zealand tour.India’s Test squad: Shubman Gill (c), Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul (vc), Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant (wk)*, Dhruv Jurel (wk), Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep, Sai Sudharsan, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj.India’s ODI squad for the first three ODIs: Shubman Gill (c), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (vc), KL Rahul (wk), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Ishan Kishan (wk), Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna*, Kuldeep Yadav.India’s ODI squad for fourth and fifth ODIs: Shreyas Iyer (c), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan (wk, vc], Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Kumar Kushagra (wk), Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur, Kuldeep Yadav.India tour of New Zealand – Test series fixturesNo.Start DayDateTimeMatchVenue1Thursday19-Nov-263:30 AM IST1st TestWellington2Friday27-Nov-263:30 AM IST2nd TestChristchurchStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Shubman Gill and I got along well': Lindblad on meeting India captain
articles.summary: Indian-origin Formula 1 driver Arvid Lindblad has praised teenage cricket star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and spoken about his conversations with India captain
articles.body: Indian-origin Formula 1 driver Arvid Lindblad has praised teenage cricket star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and spoken about his conversations with India captain Shubman Gill. The Racing Bulls driver met Gill at Silverstone during the 2026 Formula One season and also attended India's cricket match against England earlier this year.Lindblad described Gill as “really nice”. He said they spoke about the differences between Formula 1 and cricket and how athletes can learn from each other despite competing in different sports.Lindblad On His Conversation With GillIn an interview with NDTV, the 19-year-old was asked whether he had discussed the demands of competing at the highest level with Gill.“We spoke briefly about the differences between our sports and some of the ways he manages things," Lindblad said.He added that athletes could learn from each other, even when they compete in different sports.“One of the cool aspects of sport is that athletes can learn from each other, but we didn't have a particularly deep conversation. It was a fairly short interaction.”'He's Obviously Very Impressive': Lindblad On SooryavanshiLindblad also spoke about the rise of teenage cricket sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. He praised the youngster for performing on a big stage at such a young age.“He's obviously very impressive. It's amazing to see someone so young performing on such a big stage," Lindblad said.When asked why young athletes across different sports were making their mark so early, Lindblad pointed to improvements in technology, coaching and preparation.“Maybe it's the rajma or something!” he joked, before adding that improvements in technology, coaching and preparation were helping young athletes learn faster than ever.Praising Sooryavanshi's achievements, Lindblad said: “What Vaibhav has achieved is particularly remarkable. To make a name for yourself at that age is extremely impressive, and I wish him all the best,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Deepti Sharma, debutant Niki Prasad rescue India after top-order collapse against Zimbabwe
articles.summary: Experienced Deepti Sharma and debutant Niki Prasad helped India recover from a top-order collapse to secure a four-wicket win over Zimbabwe in the first
articles.body: Experienced Deepti Sharma and debutant Niki Prasad helped India recover from a top-order collapse to secure a four-wicket win over Zimbabwe in the first T20I in Raipur on Friday.India had to work harder than expected while chasing a target of 115, but recovered from losing four wickets for just 19 runs to reach the target with 4.2 overs to spare.Smriti Mandhana began her first match as India's full-time T20I captain with a couple of boundaries, but her dismissal triggered a collapse that left India struggling at 19 for 4 in the fourth over.Mandhana fell for one in the second over, followed by Anushka Sharma. Harmanpreet Kaur's wicket left India at 19 for 3 before Shafali Verma was dismissed at the same score, leaving the hosts in trouble inside the powerplay.Nyasha Gwanzura played a key role in the collapse, dismissing Mandhana, Anushka and Shafali with her offspin, while Michelle Mavunga sent Harmanpreet back to the pavilion. Zimbabwe, who had lost all 18 of their T20Is this year, suddenly had a chance to pull off an upset.However, Deepti and debutant Niki had other plans.Deepti scored 49 off 37 balls, while Niki made 39 off 35 as the pair put together an 82-run partnership for the fifth wicket to bring India back into the contest and put them on course for victory.Niki eventually sealed the win with a boundary, with India reaching the target with 4.2 overs to spare. It was a challenging start to her international career, with the youngster walking in when India were in deep trouble before helping guide them to victory.Earlier, Zimbabwe had reached 60 for 1 after 10 overs, with Kelis Ndhlovu looking comfortable at the crease. India’s bowlers then kept the scoring in check through the middle overs. World No. 1 N Shree Charani finished with figures of 1 for 14, while Nandani Sharma took two wickets in the final over to end with 2 for 11.Ndhlovu scored 42, while Sharne Mayers added an unbeaten 43 to help Zimbabwe finish at 114 for 5.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Under pressure and on the move: Morkel flags mental fatigue in Indian camp amid 'jam-packed' schedule
articles.summary: India's fast bowling coach Morne Morkel on Friday praised the bowlers for continuing to deliver for the team despite the “mental fatigue” caused by a
articles.body: India's fast bowling coach Morne Morkel on Friday praised the bowlers for continuing to deliver for the team despite the “mental fatigue” caused by a packed schedule.Indian cricketers have had a busy couple of months, playing several bilateral series as well as competing at the Asian Games in Japan.“I read everything that's written on social media. One thing that we sometimes forget is that mental fatigue plays a big part. We have to manage that and you have to be smart with it. If you look at this T20 side, some of the players went for the Asian Games, and then went straight into a full series now (vs the West Indies),” Morkel said on the eve of the fifth T20I in Bengaluru.“Then they had to fly off to Delhi for a presentation there (meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi) and back here in the morning. And, now, we have to get them ready for a game. So, that is the reality and these guys are also human,” he added.Morkel stressed that players need enough time to recover between matches to perform at their best.“And for me, your execution and your skills will be better when you've recovered well, when you've slept well, and once you've mentally refreshed and that is a challenge. We're going to fly now to New Zealand. It's a jam-packed schedule there as well.”With another busy schedule ahead, the former South African fast bowler urged people to be measured in their criticism of the team's bowling performances.“And that is sometimes a tricky thing. So, I've got a lot of respect for these guys, with the performances that they are at the moment producing for Team India, with the schedule we have.“You know, and that's why I sometimes think we can allow them to make a mistake and allow them to have an off game and not be on them, because of the mental load and expectation on these players,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs West Indies: Rain threat looms over T20I series decider in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru: Evening showers over the past few days have kept Bengaluru drenched, and the forecast offers little respite over the weekend.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Evening showers over the past few days have kept Bengaluru drenched, and the forecast offers little respite over the weekend. That is hardly welcome news ahead of the India-West Indies T20I series decider on Saturday night, with rain threatening a contest that promises plenty of fireworks.With the high-scoring series locked at 2-2, both teams will be desperately hoping for a full game. For India, there is an added incentive: they have not lost a home bilateral T20I series since Feb 2019.The opening match saw India chase down a modest target of 172 with eight wickets to spare, but the contest has taken a different turn since. The next three matches have produced a staggering 1,403 runs in 118 overs, with the batters dominating and the bowlers struggling to keep a lid on the scoring.The second match in Ranchi was a reality check for India’s bowling attack. West Indies chased down a target of 250, exposing the vulnerability of an attack missing Jasprit Bumrah. The series has underlined how crucial both Bumrah and Hardik Pandya are to India’s T20 plans.Arshdeep Singh has delivered at key moments, notably in Indore, but the pace attack has lacked consistency. When the quicks have leaked runs in the Powerplay, the spinners have been left to contain the damage, often without success.Arshdeep, who took a blow to his bowling shoulder from a Shamar Joseph bouncer in the previous match in Hyderabad, remains a doubt. The addition of Bhuvneshwar Kumar to the squad could prove a timely boost for the hosts.The 36-year-old is no stranger to the Chinnaswamy, where he made his T20I debut against Pakistan. Although his last T20I appearance came against New Zealand in Napier in Nov 2022, he has since enjoyed considerable success with RCB in the IPL.Bowling coach Morne Morkel did not rule out Arshdeep’s participation. “He (Arshdeep) is recovering well, so I think he is definitely not ruled out and is still available. Also, I am very excited to have Bhuvneshwar back in the mix,” he said.While India’s bowling has come under scrutiny, the batting has not been without its shortcomings. Even amid the run-fests, they have struggled to sustain their momentum.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We’ve sent a strong message’: Daren Sammy on West Indies’ rise ahead of India decider
articles.summary: Bengaluru: A decade ago, T20 cricket conjured images of Chris Gayle, Dwayne Bravo and Evin Lewis.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A decade ago, T20 cricket conjured images of Chris Gayle, Dwayne Bravo and Evin Lewis. Few will forget how Marlon Samuels and Carlos Brathwaite lit up the Eden Gardens as West Indies stormed to the ICC World T20 title in 2016.The road has never been easy for Caribbean cricket. The lure of franchise leagues and their lucrative pay packages has complicated the task of keeping its best players available for international duty. The players can hardly be blamed. Just before their tour of India began last month, Cricket West Indies announced a 25% cut in international players’ retainer fees and suspended this year’s men’s Super50 and women’s T20 Blaze tournaments because of a financial crunch.Against that backdrop, their 1-2 defeat in the ODI series was far from dispiriting. They have since taken the five-match T20I series to the decider. Head coach Daren Sammy, captain of the 2016 World T20-winning side, put it that it was “box-office TV stuff”.“For us, what success means may be different to the viewers,” said the former allrounder. “For us, success is progress. In spite of all the challenges that we face, if we could come here and compete against the best team in the world – the defending champs – we tick boxes that keep us in the conversation.”Sammy said the players had refused to let setbacks define them. “Before the series started, we all knew the big cuts and everything that happened. We’re still doing well and continue to be a team that brings entertainment to the world when we are doing well. It’s not because of us, it’s in spite of all the challenges that we face. The way we’ve played, we’ve sent a strong message. If we could be consistent, the players that we have in the dressing room, they go out there and give their all. When they do that, we can compete and win games against anybody in the world.”For Sammy, West Indies’ value extends beyond results. Their brand of cricket, he believes, still draws viewers and lifts spirits across the Caribbean. “The fact that we make cricket really competitive is good for viewership. When the West Indies does well, it lightens the mood of every person in the Caribbean,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kumar Kushagra, Yash Thakur earn maiden ODI call-ups for New Zealand tour
articles.summary: Mumbai: Fast bowler Prasidh Krishna, sidelined by a left hamstring injury sustained during the home ODI series against West Indies, has been picked for
articles.body: Mumbai: Fast bowler Prasidh Krishna, sidelined by a left hamstring injury sustained during the home ODI series against West Indies, has been picked for the first three ODIs and the subsequent two-Test series in New Zealand, subject to fitness clearance. The injury is understood to be minor.Wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant, who missed the India A tour of New Zealand due to a side strain and back stiffness sustained during the Irani Cup, has also been included in the Test squad, subject to fitness clearance.ODI vice-captain Shreyas Iyer will lead the side in the final two matches of the five-game series, allowing regular skipper Shubman Gill to focus on the Tests. As part of the selectors’ split-squad strategy, left-handed batter Tilak Varma and Jammu & Kashmir pacer Auqib Nabi have been drafted in for the last two ODIs.Jharkhand wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra, recently named as Pant’s replacement in the India A squad for the New Zealand tour, and fast bowler Yash Thakur have received maiden ODI call-ups. Ishan Kishan will serve as vice-captain for the final two matches.Jasprit Bumrah has been rested from the ODI series but will lead the pace attack in the Tests, which begin in Wellington on Nov 19.Seamer Anshul Kamboj, who played one Test in Manchester during the 2025 England tour before being dropped, has been recalled to the Test squad and the squad for the first three ODIs. His selection suggests the selectors continue to view him as a seam-bowling allrounder at No. 8.Akash Deep has also returned to the Test squad after being sidelined for seven months with a stress fracture. He last played a Test during the 2025 England series.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Very unfair': R Ashwin vents out frustration after India leave Yashasvi Jaiswal out of New Zealand ODIs
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin has criticised the BCCI selection committee for leaving Yashasvi Jaiswal out of India's ODI squad for the New Zealand series.
articles.body: Ravichandran Ashwin has criticised the BCCI selection committee for leaving Yashasvi Jaiswal out of India's ODI squad for the New Zealand series. The former India spinner believes Jaiswal deserved a chance in the final two matches, especially with Shubman Gill being rested.Ashwin warned that repeatedly missing out on international cricket could affect the young batter's confidence and development.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin called the decision "unfair and unfortunate". He argued that while Jaiswal may need time to prepare for the upcoming Test series, the selectors could still have included him in the last two ODIs to give him valuable match practice."If Shubman Gill is not playing the last two ODIs, then Yashasvi Jaiswal should definitely get that spot. It is very unfortunate because all of this can ruin his confidence. Now, with the way he was scoring runs..."Ashwin also pointed out that Jaiswal had not played international cricket for around four months, despite previously scoring runs consistently across formats. He said the team management should make efforts to keep a talented player involved rather than leave him without opportunities."He was a run machine. If his confidence is getting ruined, it is the job of the team management and selectors to give him an opportunity wherever possible. But he has not been getting those opportunities at all. It has not gone to him. And it is very unfair."Ashwin calls Jaiswal a precious talentAshwin suggested that the selectors could have spoken directly to Jaiswal about playing the final two ODIs, allowing him to decide whether he was ready. He acknowledged the importance of preparing for Test cricket but questioned why that should come at the cost of ODI opportunities."I agree that he needs to prepare for Test cricket. But tell me, when did Yashasvi Jaiswal last play an ODI? When did he last play a T20? When did he last play a Test match?"Jaiswal's limited ODI experience has also raised questions about India's preparations for next year's ODI World Cup in South Africa, particularly regarding the development of backup players. Ashwin stressed that the selectors and team management must take responsibility for supporting the young batter and helping him regain his rhythm."It is very unfortunate. It is definitely the responsibility of the selectors and team management to look after Yashasvi Jaiswal. He is a precious talent," Ashwin concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Idolised them for years': Rachin Ravindra reveals how Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma have shaped his batting
articles.summary: For Rachin Ravindra, the journey from an awe-struck youngster sharing the field with his cricketing idols to an established international allrounder has
articles.body: For Rachin Ravindra, the journey from an awe-struck youngster sharing the field with his cricketing idols to an established international allrounder has been one of learning, resilience and quiet evolution. Yet, even as the New Zealand batter continues to carve his own identity, the influence of Indian greats Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma remains etched into his game.With Kohli and Rohit set to feature in the upcoming ODI series against New Zealand, Ravindra acknowledged how the duo has inspired generations across the cricketing world. “Everyone around the world who has followed cricket will be crazy about Rohit and Virat. I certainly am, too. They have done it for such a long time, won trophies and remained consistent while creating some fantastic moments. They are two players I have idolised for years, modelled parts of my batting on and learnt little things from,” Ravindra said.For Ravindra, Kohli’s mastery in bouncy conditions and Rohit’s command against spin offer valuable lessons in adaptability, temperament and intent. “Watching the way Virat plays in bouncy conditions and the way Rohit plays spin has influenced me in several ways. Beyond technique, it is about their grit and determination. Kohli’s hundreds in challenging situations and Rohit’s free-flowing, fearless approach at the top are qualities I try to take from both. So, picking their brains a little bit over the years has been fantastic,” he said.Ravindra’s own breakthrough came during the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, where he amassed 578 runs at an average of 64.22. Kohli finished with 765 runs and Rohit with 594.The remarkable campaign brought Ravindra into cricket’s next celebrated elite. However, the 26-year-old doesn’t want to overthink such comparisons. “It is a privilege to be mentioned in that conversation, but the original Fab Four are streets ahead of us at the moment. Their records are fantastic, and they remain great players and idols of mine. Ultimately, my priority is to contribute to the team. That matters more than individual accolades or the number of runs I score,” he said.New Zealand, meanwhile, will draw confidence from their historic 3-0 Test series triumph in India last year. Ravindra believes that victory, achieved against a formidable home side, will strengthen the Black Caps’ belief.“Beating such a quality team in its own conditions gives you enormous confidence. Previous tours to India were difficult, and sometimes we were fortunate to win a session, rather than a match. To win three games against a side featuring Rohit, Virat, Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja was a proud moment,” he said.(Watch India tour of New Zealand live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV starting Oct 22, 2026)Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Absolute joke': Jonny Bairstow blasts ECB's decision to snub youngster George Hill for England Lions
articles.summary: Former England wicketkeeper Jonny Bairstow has strongly criticised England and the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) for leaving Yorkshire all-rounder
articles.body: Former England wicketkeeper Jonny Bairstow has strongly criticised England and the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) for leaving Yorkshire all-rounder George Hill out of the latest England Lions squads.Bairstow believes Hill’s performances and ability to contribute in all departments make him deserving of an opportunity at the international level.The 25-year-old has been overlooked for both the T20 and 50-over squads set to face West Indies A in St Kitts and Nevis in November. Bairstow, who played alongside Hill at Yorkshire, voiced his frustration through Instagram Stories on Friday."What does [George Hill] have to do!!! Averages 18 with 48 wickets and 750 runs @ 34! England are hardly blessed with people that can swing the ball, bat well and be a jet in the field!" He wrote. "Absolute joke!"Bairstow, who represented England between 2011 and 2024, highlighted Hill’s all-round skills, including his ability to take wickets, contribute runs and perform well in the field.Hill made his first-class debut in 2020 and has maintained a batting average of 31 in the format. He has also taken 178 wickets at an average of 21 runs. However, his numbers in one-day and T20 cricket have been less impressive.The Yorkshire all-rounder had previously earned a call-up to the England Lions squad in May 2025, but he has not been included in either of the latest white-ball squads.England Lions prepare for West Indies AThe England Lions are scheduled to play three T20 matches and five 50-over games against West Indies A in November. The squads feature several young players, including Rehan Ahmed, Ben McKinney, Thomas Rew and James Rew.Hill’s omission has drawn attention to the selectors’ decision, with Bairstow making it clear that he believes the all-rounder’s performances should have earned him a place in the squads.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ravindra Jadeja, Yashasvi Jaiswal dropped! India’s big ODI calls ahead of 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: India’s ODI plans for the 2027 World Cup continue to evolve, with the selectors making several changes to the squads for the upcoming five-match series
articles.body: India’s ODI plans for the 2027 World Cup continue to evolve, with the selectors making several changes to the squads for the upcoming five-match series against New Zealand. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Friday announced separate squads for the first three and final two matches, with the split aimed at giving Test regulars time to prepare for the two-match red-ball series, which begins just four days after the ODIs.The selections have raised questions over the futures of some established players, with Ravindra Jadeja emerging as the biggest omission from the squad for the first three matches. The veteran allrounder has struggled for form over the past several months, and his exclusion could be a significant setback to his hopes of making India’s squad for the 2027 World Cup.Axar Patel has been brought in as a like-for-like replacement for Jadeja. The left-arm allrounder last played an ODI in July against England and will now have an opportunity to strengthen his case for a place in the team for the marquee tournament in Africa.Another notable omission is Yashasvi Jaiswal, who has been left out of both squads for the New Zealand series. The decision means the opener will miss an opportunity to partner Rohit Sharma at the top of the order after Shubman Gill leaves the ODI squad to prepare for the Tests. Gill is set to depart after the first two matches. The BCCI has not provided an explanation for Jaiswal’s exclusion.Wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel has also been left out and replaced by Ishan Kishan, despite not getting an opportunity to play in the first four ODIs against West Indies. Kishan, along with Shreyas Iyer and Arshdeep Singh, returns to the fold after missing the West Indies series due to the 2026 Asian Games.There has also been a change in the pace department. Auqib Nabi, who featured in the first ODI against West Indies in Guwahati, conceded 84 runs without taking a wicket and has been replaced by Anshul Kamboj for the first three matches against New Zealand. The arrangement will be reversed for the final two ODIs, with Kamboj leaving for Test preparations and Nabi returning to the squad.The squad will undergo further changes after the first three ODIs, with Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Anshul Kamboj and Prasidh Krishna leaving to focus on preparations for the Test series.Tilak Varma will join the squad for the final two matches, along with Kumar Kushagra and Yash Thakur, who are set to make their ODI debuts. Auqib Nabi will also return for the last two games.Players leaving after the first three ODIs: Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Anshul Kamboj and Prasidh Krishna.Players joining for the fourth and fifth ODIs: Tilak Varma, Auqib Nabi, Kumar Kushagra and Yash Thakur.India’s ODI squad for the first three ODIs: Shubman Gill [C], Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer [VC], KL Rahul [WK], Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Ishan Kishan [WK], Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna*, Kuldeep YadavIndia’s ODI squad for fourth and fifth ODIs: Shreyas Iyer [C], Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan [WK, VC], Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Kumar Kushagra [WK], Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur, Kuldeep YadavStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Delhi Capitals' big IPL 2027 shake-up continues, Sri Lanka legend joins Sourav Ganguly's team
articles.summary: Former Sri Lanka all-rounder Chaminda Vaas is set for his maiden coaching stint in the Indian Premier League after being appointed Delhi Capitals' fast
articles.body: Former Sri Lanka all-rounder Chaminda Vaas is set for his maiden coaching stint in the Indian Premier League after being appointed Delhi Capitals' fast bowling coach ahead of the 2027 season.Vaas, one of Sri Lanka's most successful fast bowlers, claimed 355 wickets in Tests and 400 in ODIs during his international career. He joins a revamped Capitals coaching staff headed by former India captain Sourav Ganguly, with former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh having been appointed assistant and batting coach earlier this week.The 52-year-old replaces former India pacer Munaf Patel, who served as Delhi's bowling coach over the previous two seasons.Vaas brings considerable international coaching experience to the role. He has worked with Sri Lanka's men's team in three separate stints and also had a brief coaching contract with New Zealand. He was appointed Sri Lanka's bowling coach from 2013 to 2015 before taking up the same role with Ireland for the 2016 T20 World Cup. He subsequently returned to the Sri Lankan set-up.The former left-arm pacer is also familiar with the IPL, having represented Deccan Chargers between 2008 and 2010. He picked up 18 wickets in 13 matches for the franchise.Vaas' appointment is the latest development in Delhi Capitals' preparations for the 2027 season, as the franchise continues to reshape its backroom staff under Ganguly's leadership.Delhi have also been active in the player trade market in recent months. Pacer T Natarajan moved back to Sunrisers Hyderabad from Delhi, with spinner Zeeshan Ansari heading in the opposite direction. Natarajan, acquired by Delhi for Rs 10.75 crore at the 2025 auction, moved to SRH at a revised fee of Rs 5 crore, while Ansari joined the Capitals at his existing fee of Rs 40 lakh.In another major trade announced months ago, wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant returned to Delhi Capitals from Lucknow Super Giants, while left-arm spinner Kuldeep Yadav moved to Lucknow. Pant, who spent nine seasons with Delhi from 2016 to 2024, took a pay cut from his Rs 27 crore auction price at LSG to Rs 15 crore for his return to the franchise.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'India need to get Shai Hope out': Nayar suggests change in tactics against Windies skipper
articles.summary: Former Indian cricketer Abhishek Nayar stated that India would need to get Shai Hope out, as the West Indies captain has been tormenting the bowling
articles.body: Former Indian cricketer Abhishek Nayar stated that India would need to get Shai Hope out, as the West Indies captain has been tormenting the bowling attack and winning matches almost single-handedly.Hope has been in stellar form in the ongoing white-ball series against India, having scored four centuries across three ODIs and four T20Is, often proving to be the difference between the two sides.India have lost all three matches in which they failed to dismiss Hope during the ongoing white-ball series, with the batter scoring unbeaten centuries in each of them. With the T20I series locked at 2-2 ahead of Saturday's decider in Bengaluru, Nayar said the Men in Blue need to find a way to dismiss Hope and suggested strategies they could employ to remove him early."The West Indies have batted well, and in the previous match, they bowled well too. But you have to find a way to get Shai Hope out. You have to find a way to stop the West Indies from scoring runs in the powerplay, and that's where the think tank comes together, plans, makes strategies, and puts all that together; then you can get the result you desire," Nayar told JioStar.Hope has scored 539 runs in seven white-ball innings, including four centuries. His 261 runs in four T20Is are already the most by any visiting batter in a bilateral series in India, reflecting his dominance throughout the tour."After a long time, such a player has come to India, scoring runs, captaining, wicket-keeping as well, and consistently scoring runs with the bat. When he scores runs, the team wins, and that is the hallmark of a terrific and great player who scores runs and makes sure the team wins. He is using his craft and finesse as well as power, and that is one thing that Shai Hope has done brilliantly," Nayar said while praising Hope.Nayar also suggested that India should vary their lines and lengths against Hope, who has found deliveries aimed at the stumps easy to score off."When you are bowling at the stumps, it's been very easy for him to score runs, which means sometimes inconsistency is the best consistency to have against Shai Hope."That is something India will have to think about and come up with a plan as to how they are going to make sure that he starts playing more behind square and how they start using the short ball more against him," he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has remained on the bench for all four T20Is against the West Indies, with India preferring the opening combination of Sanju Samson
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has remained on the bench for all four T20Is against the West Indies, with India preferring the opening combination of Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma.India head coach Gautam Gambhir has backed the current opening pair, saying dropping either Samson or Abhishek to accommodate Sooryavanshi would be unfair. He pointed to Samson’s ability and past performances, including his Player of the Tournament award at the World Cup."I think Samson showed what he is capable of. Someone doesn't become Player Of The Tournament in the World Cup without having talent, so he has done enough. Obviously, it was tough- probably the toughest decision I have taken in my coaching career, was leaving him out of that England series because of the way he had performed before that," said Gambhir.He added that a few poor performances do not make established players less capable, particularly those who helped India win the World Cup. Gambhir said the team wanted to return to the combination that had worked during the tournament.Ahead of the fifth ODI, the 15-year-old batter has shared a cryptic social media post saying "still believing", suggesting he remains hopeful of getting an opportunity in the fifth and final match as India look to win the series.Sooryavanshi assured of a longer runGambhir acknowledged the teenager’s talent but stressed that he must wait for his chance, with experienced players currently ahead of him in the selection order."From Vaibhav's point of view, it is again a very clear conversation that he has to wait for his opportunity. We know the kind of talent he has. We know what he can do. But again, someone who done extremely well over a period of years obviously will always be ahead of someone who has got into the team. Whenever he gets that chance, you will get a longer run as well," he explained.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Very tempted to play Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’: Ex-India coach’s big call for series decider
articles.summary: India are set to face the West Indies in the fifth and final T20I in Bengaluru on Saturday, with the series locked at 2-2.
articles.body: India are set to face the West Indies in the fifth and final T20I in Bengaluru on Saturday, with the series locked at 2-2. Ahead of the decider, former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar has backed Sanju Samson to carry his confidence from the previous match into the series finale, while weighing in on the possibility of including teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in the playing XI.Speaking on JioHotstar's ‘Game Plan’, Nayar praised Samson's approach in the fourth T20I, saying the wicketkeeper-batter appeared to be back in his rhythm and could play a decisive role if he spends more time at the crease.'Dangerous Sanju was back in his rhythm'Nayar felt Samson's start in the fourth T20I was particularly encouraging, with the batter looking settled and in control at the crease."In the beginning, it was a very good strategic call, with Sanju Samson taking the strike. After that, the way he was batting, it felt like he was setting himself up for a big one because he was in control. His base was good, along with control, and his head was steady. It felt like that dangerous Sanju was back in his rhythm in the last game. He will take this confidence into Bengaluru, and I feel this Indian team will be in a much better position because a lot of the batters are in form. It's only a matter of them delivering together," Nayar said.India could not convert the promising start into a victory, but Nayar believes Samson's innings offered encouragement heading into the series decider. He also pointed out that while Abhishek Sharma was not at his best, Samson stepped up to give India the momentum they needed."Yes, Abhishek Sharma wasn't in his greatest of flows, but Sanju Samson took over. That start, even though India didn't get that result, is invaluable because you could get close. So, you want to take that confidence going forward and say, if Sanju can bat for a few more overs, then in the next game, India will be sitting pretty in making sure they win the series 3-2."Nayar tempted by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, but favours bowling changesWith the series on the line, India could consider changes to their playing XI. However, Nayar believes the team management faces a difficult decision, particularly if it considers bringing in 15-year-old Sooryavanshi.The youngster's inclusion would raise questions about the batting order, as Nayar feels Sooryavanshi should be used as an opener rather than being asked to bat outside his strongest position."I think India are in a Catch-22 situation. I'll take a punt and try and go the Kuldeep Yadav way. So, I may replace Naman Dhir with Kuldeep Yadav and get Nitish and Axar one place up. Axar Patel has also played that role of a floater really well for Team India when he has been sent up," he said.Nayar admitted that he was keen to see Sooryavanshi feature in Bengaluru, given the conditions at the venue. However, he stressed that selecting the youngster would require a reshuffle at the top of the order, potentially affecting other batters' roles."I am very tempted to play Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. But are you going to play him out of position? If Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is playing, then he plays in his strongest position, which is opening. And if he is opening, then whoever is number three should also be playing in his strongest position. However tempted I may be to see Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, that too in Bengaluru in such good conditions, I will make changes in the bowling, not in the batting at all," Nayar added.His preferred option is to strengthen the bowling attack by bringing in Kuldeep Yadav, potentially at the expense of Naman Dhir, while moving Nitish Reddy and Axar Patel up one position. The suggestion would allow India to make a tactical adjustment without disturbing the existing batting combination.India, will have to assess the availability of Arshdeep Singh, who suffered a blow to his left shoulder during the fourth T20I in Hyderabad. Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been added to the squad, with a decision on his participation to be taken before the match based on his recovery.With the series evenly poised, India will be looking to secure a 3-2 victory on home soil, while the West Indies have an opportunity to claim a series win in India.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mumbai Indians, Mahela Jayawardene mutually agree to bring in 'fresh perspective'; new coach likely
articles.summary: Mumbai Indians and head coach Mahela Jayawardene have mutually decided to bring in a fresh perspective starting with the upcoming Indian Premier League
articles.body: Mumbai Indians and head coach Mahela Jayawardene have mutually decided to bring in a fresh perspective starting with the upcoming Indian Premier League season. In a meeting of the top brass earlier this week, both parties reached an agreement. TimesofIndia.com has learnt that a new head coach is likely to be finalised soon.The IPL giants have already identified multiple candidates for the top job and interviews could happen in the coming week to finalise the new head coach.
